verses.text: David called all the leaders of Israel to meet in Jerusalem. He called the leaders of the tribes, the commanders of the army groups that served the king, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, the officials in charge of all the property and animals that belonged to the king and his sons, the palace officials, the mighty men, and all the brave warriors.

King David stood up and said, "Listen to me, my relatives and my people. I wanted to build a house as a resting place for the ark of the LORD's covenant, a footstool for our God, and I made plans to build it.
But God said to me, 'You will not build a house to honour my name, because you are a warrior and have spilled blood.'

Still, the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from my whole family to be king over Israel forever. He chose the tribe of Judah to lead, and from Judah he chose my father's family. From my father's sons he was pleased to make me king over all Israel.
The LORD has given me many sons, and from all of them he has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the LORD's kingdom over Israel.
He said to me, 'Your son Solomon is the one who will build my house and my courtyards. I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father.
I will make his kingdom last forever, if he keeps on obeying my commands and rules as he does now.'

So now, in front of all Israel, the LORD's assembly, and with our God listening, I tell you: Be careful to obey all the commands of the LORD your God. Then you will keep this good land and pass it on to your children after you forever.

And you, my son Solomon, know the God of your father. Serve him with all your heart and a willing mind, because the LORD looks into every heart and understands every plan and thought. If you look for him, you will find him. But if you turn away from him, he will reject you forever.
Remember this: the LORD has chosen you to build a house to be his holy place. Be strong and do the work."
Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the porch of the temple, its buildings, its storerooms, its upstairs rooms, its inner rooms, and the room for the atonement cover.

He gave him the plans for everything the Spirit had put in his mind: the courtyards of the LORD's temple, all the rooms around it, the treasuries of God's temple, and the treasuries for the gifts set apart for God.
He gave him instructions for the groups of priests and Levites, for all the work of serving in the LORD's temple, and for all the objects to be used in its service.
He told him how much gold to use for all the gold objects used in each kind of service, and how much silver for all the silver objects used in each kind of service.

He told him how much gold to use for the gold lampstands and their lamps, by weight for each lampstand and its lamps. He also told him how much silver to use for each silver lampstand and its lamps, according to how each lampstand would be used.
He told him how much gold to use for each table for the holy bread, and how much silver for the silver tables.
He told him how much pure gold to use for the meat forks, the sprinkling bowls, and the pitchers, and how much gold and silver for each gold and silver dish.
He told him how much refined gold to use for the altar of incense. He also gave him the plan for the chariot, the gold cherubim that spread their wings over the ark of the LORD's covenant.
David said, "All this is written down from the LORD's own hand to me. He helped me understand all the details of the plan."

David also said to his son Solomon, "Be strong and brave, and do the work. Do not be afraid or lose heart, because the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not fail you or abandon you until all the work for the service of the LORD's temple is finished.

Look, the groups of priests and Levites are ready for all the service of God's temple. Every willing person with skill for any kind of work will help you. The leaders and all the people will do everything you command."
